articles.title: OCTOBER 2008
articles.summary: This document presents a calendar for October 2008, detailing astronomical events like Moon phases and the Orionids meteor shower, alongside significant anniversaries in space exploration, such as the launch of GOES-1 and the first photo of the Moon's far side by Lunik 3. It integrates various educational themes, including energy awareness and World Space Week, consistently encouraging engagement with NASA's "The Space Place" website for related activities and information.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky: Twinkle, Twinkle
articles.summary: This article offers an astronomical guide for October, detailing opportunities to observe various celestial bodies like the Moon, Venus, Jupiter, Neptune, Uranus, and the asteroid Vesta. It provides specific viewing times and tips, including how to locate these objects. A key focus is on explaining why planets appear not to twinkle compared to stars, attributing this phenomenon to their disk size relative to atmospheric fluctuations, and notes exceptions like Pluto.

articles.title: Death of a Supergiant
articles.summary: NASA researchers are developing "Sensor Web 2.0," a web portal akin to a "Google for satellites," designed to simplify access to data from Earth-observing satellites. This system allows users to easily request specific information, such as wildfire maps or floodwater salinity, and can even trigger satellites to acquire new imagery in an area of interest. The initiative aims to integrate numerous satellites into a seamless, user-friendly network to enhance our ability to observe and understand the planet, as demonstrated during the Myanmar cyclone crisis.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lectures
articles.summary: The article announces an upcoming Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture by Leonard Susskind on October 1st, where he will discuss "The Black Hole Wars: My Battle with Stephen Hawking," a non-technical talk exploring black hole theory and its implications for understanding reality. Additionally, it provides an overview of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), which commenced operations in September 2008, explaining its purpose in particle physics and potential discoveries such as new particles, the Higgs boson, or evidence for string theory.

articles.title: The Last 31 Days In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article, titled 'The Last 31 Days In Astronomy,' reports on several key astronomical events and discoveries from August and September 2008. Highlights include updates on the Hubble repair mission, findings from Mars rovers Phoenix and Opportunity, new details from Cassini's flyby of Enceladus, a theory on black holes forming stars, and the detection of a mysterious new type of variable celestial object.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a Telescope Loaner Program, allowing members to test various telescopes and binoculars before purchasing. The program maintains a diverse inventory, including Dobsonians, refractors, Newtonians, and Schmidt-Cassegrains, catering to all experience levels. The article also provides contact information for the club's officers, board of directors, and various club services, along with publication details for the SJAA Ephemeris newsletter.
